name: Money
description: Household finance and economics, for arguments about what people can afford.

facts.statement: About 37% of American adults could not cover a $400 emergency expense with cash
facts.short: the share of Americans without $400 spare
facts.source: US Federal Reserve, Survey of Household Economics

facts.statement: About 82% of American adults have a credit card
facts.short: the share of Americans holding a credit card
facts.source: US Federal Reserve, Survey of Household Economics

facts.statement: The average credit card interest rate in the US is about 21%
Consumer spending is about 68% of US economic output
facts.short: the share of the US economy that is people buying things

facts.statement: Only about 16% of US payments are made in cash
facts.short: the share of payments still made in cash
facts.source: Federal Reserve Diary of Consumer Payment Choice

facts.statement: The wealthiest 1% of US households hold about 31% of the country's wealth
facts.short: the share of wealth held by the top one percent

facts.statement: About 9% of the world's population lives on less than $2.15 a day
facts.short: the share of humanity in extreme poverty

facts.statement: Americans save about 4.6% of their disposable income
facts.short: the share of income Americans save

facts.statement: About half of American renters spend more than 30% of their income on rent
facts.short: the share of renters who are cost-burdened
facts.source: Harvard Joint Center for Housing Studies

facts.statement: About 28% of American non-retirees have no retirement savings at all
facts.short: the share of Americans with nothing saved for retirement

facts.statement: US consumer prices rose about 8% in 2022, the fastest in forty years

facts.statement: About half of new US businesses survive five years
